## Universal Location Reference Layout — Text Mirror of the Visual Sheet

This is the **written/visual template** of the location sheet reference (Uruk Streets style). Use it as a layout guide when generating any location reference image, or as a structural guide when describing the layout. Generic placeholders only — fill with any project's content.

---

## VISUAL DESIGN SPECIFICATIONS

**Background**: Cream (#F4ECDD) OR dark charcoal (#0A0805) depending on scene mood
**Typography**:
- Header in elegant serif uppercase
- Section labels in tiny serif caps below each plate

**Header (top strip, 3-column)**:
- LEFT: "LOCATION SHEET" in small caps serif
- CENTER: Large elegant serif uppercase location name
- RIGHT: Project title (small serif), optional episode/time of day below

**Row 1** — 4 equal angle plates of the same location from different camera positions:
1. HERO WIDE — main establishing shot, dramatic angle, deep focus
2. REVERSE ANGLE — camera flipped 180° from hero
3. DOORWAY DETAIL — mid shot showing focal architecture or entry point
4. CAMERA CORNER — alternative shooting angle for coverage

Labels in tiny serif caps below each cell.

**Row 2 LEFT (~60% width)** — Large hero shot:
- Final wide cinematic plate at the established time of day and weather
- All practical lights visible
- Consistent atmosphere

**Row 2 RIGHT (~40% width)** — SET DETAILS grid (4x2 = 8 cells):
- Material textures and props isolated cells
- Each captioned in tiny serif caps below
- Section header "SET DETAILS" at top right of this column

**Bottom strip (full width)** — Color palette:
- 8 color swatches
- Captioned in tiny serif caps below each

## REQUIRED LOCATION DETAILS FIELDS

When filling this template, define and lock the following:

- **NAME**: [location name]
- **SETTING / ERA**: [date or fictional era]
- **ARCHITECTURE / MATERIALS**: [walls, floors, ceilings/roofs, windows, doors]
- **ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS**: [time of day, weather, season]
- **LIGHT SOURCES (practicals visible in frame)**: [list each lamp, torch, window, fire pit]
- **FLORA / PROPS**: [plants, jars, fabrics, tools, weapons]
- **MOOD**: [emotional tone this location must produce]
- **TIME OF DAY**: [morning, noon, golden hour, blue hour, night]
- **WEATHER / ATMOSPHERIC EFFECTS**: [clear, rain, fog, snow, haze, smoke]
- **COLOR PALETTE**: [list 6-8 hex codes for the location]
- **CONSISTENCY ACROSS SCENES**: [what stays the same]

---

## RULES FOR USING THIS TEMPLATE

1. Use box-drawing characters for the ASCII layout.
2. Keep all 4 angle plates equal width with consistent lighting and time-of-day.
3. Hero shot occupies ~60% of the second row width; SET DETAILS grid occupies ~40%.
4. SET DETAILS grid is 4 columns x 2 rows = 8 isolated cells.
5. Color palette strip spans full width at the bottom with 8 swatches.
6. Background can be cream (museum-catalog) or dark (cinematic), depending on scene mood. The label typography follows the piece's register: the serif lettering above is the default, and a children's piece takes a rounded sans.
7. Same lighting direction and weather across all 4 angle plates.
8. SET DETAILS cells show only materials and small props, isolated on neutral background.

## END OF LOCATION SHEET TEXT-VISUAL TEMPLATE

This template is generic and reusable for any location — historical, modern, fantasy, sci-fi, interior, exterior. Fill placeholders with the project's content while keeping the visual structure identical.
